# Cloud SQL

### Known gaps

- Not served: SQL Server, failover (HA), switchover, demote and demoteMaster, DR replicas and replicationCluster, cascading replicas, cross-region and cross-project replicas, maintenance windows and reschedule, executeSql, resetSslConfig, rotateServerCa and the other certificate rotation calls, truncateLog, major version upgrade, the projects/backups resource, DNS connect settings, Auth Proxy and IAM database authentication. SQL Server is out of scope: the RDS opt-in SQL Server engine is a separate proxy-based design that was not reused.
- availabilityType REGIONAL is stored but creates no standby: the RDS Multi-AZ pattern is a record flag, so there is nothing to reuse, and a real standby needs the failover operation above.
- Settings reaching the engine: tier (CPU and memory caps), databaseFlags, activationPolicy and the PITR switches. dataDiskSizeGb and dataDiskType are echoed only (docker volumes have no quota). ipConfiguration.authorizedNetworks, sslMode and requireSsl are not enforced: the engine publishes on 127.0.0.1 only. backupConfiguration schedule (no automated backups run), maintenanceWindow, insightsConfig and passwordValidationPolicy have no effect.
- PostgreSQL ignores database charset and collation (stored only); MySQL users get GRANT ALL on *.*; PostgreSQL users join a cloudsqlsuperuser role the emulator creates. Backups keep object ownership, so restoring one into a different instance needs the same roles to exist.
- Flags are validated by the engine when the restart applies them, not when the patch is accepted; flags.list is a static subset and tiers.list a fixed list. Duplicate database and user inserts return 409 but the real reason strings were not verified against the live service.
- Docker engines need the container runtime to see the emulator's temp directory (bind mount), so a gopherstack running inside a container that talks to a remote daemon cannot export, import, back up or clone; admin SQL still works.
- Instance name reuse after delete is allowed (the real service blocks it for a week); automatic backups are not run. MySQL PITR resolution is one second and replays over replication, so the source engine must be running; PostgreSQL clones need the WAL archive volume. A PostgreSQL recovery to a time before any commit following the base fails at the engine, not at the API. The earliest-recovery bound and the error strings for a replica without binary logging, a non-replica promote and deleting a primary with replicas are unverified. crash_recovery: {status: ok, note: "Engine containers carry gopherstack.managed/owner/service/resource labels; after a crash a restart with the same data dir adopts the running container of a restored primary (same image, tier and dump directory, reachable with the persisted password) and removes the rest. Replicas, recoveries and fresh instances relaunch; the private replication network of a crashed run is not removed."}
